outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms capable of producing swaths of damaging winds and isolated large hail appear likely across parts of central and north Texas this afternoon and evening.

sections.title: Southern Plains
sections.text: An upper trough will progress eastward across the northern and central Plains today, which will suppress upper ridging centered over the southern Plains and northern Mexico. At the surface, a cold front initially extending from western Ontario into the northern/central Plains will move southward across the southern Plains through the period. Temperatures ahead of the front are forecast to warm well into the 90s across much of central and north TX, which combined with a very moist low-level airmass will support very strong instability. MLCAPE values of 3000+ J/kg appear likely by late afternoon, and may potentially reach near 4000-5000 J/kg in some areas based on RAP/NAM forecast soundings. Although low-level flow is forecast to remain weak across the southern Plains, mid and upper-level flow should gradually increase with the glancing influence of the upper trough to the north. A small convective complex over western KS early this morning should continue moving south-southeastward, and will probably be located near the KS/OK border around 12Z. sections.title: Southeast
sections.text: A moist airmass will remain over much of the Southeast today, as a weak upper low centered over KY/TN continues to fill through the period. Instability developing due to diurnal heating will favor scattered daytime storms across much of the region. Weak shear and poor mid-level lapse rates will likely limit the potential for this convection to become organized, but occasional gusty winds cannot be completely ruled out with the strongest storms.

sections.title: Dakotas
sections.text: Cold mid-level temperatures (around -24 to -25C at 500 mb) will be present over the Dakotas this afternoon. Isolated to perhaps widely scattered afternoon thunderstorms may form in a post-frontal environment beneath the upper trough. At this time, the forecast elevated instability appears rather weak, but small hail and gusty winds could occur on an isolated basis. ..Gleason/Dean.. 06/09/2019

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Over the CONUS, substantial pattern transition is underway in mid/upper levels, as a high builds over the TX/MX border region and a broad/long-lasting trough essentially weakens in place over the Southeast. A high-amplitude synoptic-scale trough is evident in moisture-channel imagery from a cyclone over Nunavut southward across central Canada then southwestward across the Dakotas WY and eastern UT. The U.S. portion of that trough will move eastward to the upper Mississippi Valley, IA and northeastern KS by the end of the period. The associated surface cold front was analyzed at 11Z from northeastern MN to northwestern MO, central KS, the TX Panhandle, and east-central NM. This front should move eastward over the upper Mississippi Valley by 00Z, while moving southward across the southern Plains to southeastern OK and north-central through southwest TX. The front will overtake a dryline mixing eastward through the day across west-central/southwest TX. A wave low appears probable over northwest/north-central TX, shifting into central TX through this evening, at the generally southward- propagating intersection of the front and an outflow boundary. The latter boundary still is progress

sections.title: North/central TX to southern OK and southwest TX
sections.text: Though isolated severe hail/gusts may be noted this morning through midday with convection near the outflow boundary, the more-organized severe threat will be farther south this afternoon into evening. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms should erupt quickly during mid- late afternoon from north-central into central TX, with additional development possible southward near the Balcones Escarpment and southwestward over parts of the Edwards Plateau near the front. Severe wind gusts and sporadic large hail are expected. Some potential exists for cold-pool aggregation and an organized cold pool, forward-propagating southward to south-southeastward into a well-mixed, high-CAPE environment with a swath of severe wind. Though mesoscale uncertainties exist with regard to the speed and depth of the prefrontal/convective cold pool and outflow/front intersection, low-level convergence will be maximized near the wave low, as well as along adjoining segments of the front and outflow boundary. sections.title: TX through late evening
sections.text: An initially elevated thunderstorm cluster over central OK has evolved into a small MCS with a well-defined cold pool and several measured severe gusts. The outflow with this MCS is becoming the effective cold front across southern OK, while the strong synoptic cold front is surging south-southeastward across northwest and west central TX. VWP data from TLX shows a cold pool depth of 2-3 km above ground level, which suggests that the outflow boundary will continue to focus new storm development southward through the afternoon as the low levels destabilize across TX. Storms should also form along the synoptic cold front farther to the west and southwest later this afternoon. South-east of these boundaries, strong surface heating and boundary-layer dewpoints in the low-mid 70s, beneath midlevel lapse rates in excess of 9 C/km, will drive strong buoyancy (MLCAPE in excess of 3000 J/kg). Though deep-layer flow/shear will be on the lower margins for organized severe storms, the large buoyancy and steep lapse rates will support DCAPE approaching 1500 J/kg, which will favor intense downdrafts and damaging wind potential in the stronger cores. sections.title: FL this afternoon
sections.text: A weak midlevel trough persists from the TN Valley to the northeast Gulf of Mexico, with deep southwesterly flow over the FL peninsula. Rich low-level moisture and slight cooling aloft compared to yesterday, along with daytime heating, will contribute to moderate buoyancy this afternoon across parts of central/south FL. The favored zone for a few stronger storms with gusty outflow winds and marginally severe hail will be where inland convective clusters merge with the Atlantic coast sea breeze along the east central and southeast FL coast. ..Thompson/Squitieri.. 06/09/2019

sections.title: TX update
sections.text: A long-lived but small MCS continues to travel quickly southward through north TX, now through the Metroplex with embedded large hail and damaging winds. Given the intensity of the eastern cells, have expanded severe probabilities southeastward to account for a possible continuation along the instability gradient toward southeast TX with wind and hail threat. Western portions of the outflow boundary have merged with the main wind shift over northwest TX ahead of the surging cold front. All areas south of these boundaries continue to destabilize, with very strong instability in place capable of supporting robust updrafts. In addition to along the southward-surging outflow, additional development is expected to the west where a large CU field has developed. One or more southward moving MCSs are expected, with swaths of potentially destructive winds. ..Jewell.. 06/09/2019 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1124 AM CDT Sun Jun 09 2019/

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms mainly producing scattered damaging winds and isolated large hail will continue across parts of central into south Texas this evening.

sections.title: TX
sections.text: A bowing line of storms producing damaging winds will continue generally southward over south-central TX this evening. Isolated large hail and perhaps a brief tornado will also be possible with supercells embedded within the line, but scattered damaging winds remain the primary threat. The airmass immediately ahead of this convection remains strongly unstable, with MLCAPE likely around 2500-3000 J/kg or greater. Primary uncertainty remains how far south this line will maintain its intensity. 00Z soundings from CRP and DRT show a strongly unstable surface-based parcel, but convective inhibition will increase this evening with the loss of daytime heating. Still, current expectations are for the line to remain capable of producing damaging winds over the next few hours (until at least 03-04Z), and significant severe gusts remain possible in the short term between Austin and San Antonio. There may be some tendency for the line to develop south-southwestward into the area of maximum instability this evening, and severe probabilities have been adjusted to account for this possibility. mesoscale_discussions.summary: An MCS is expected to progress southward towards Texas over the next few hours. Large hail is the main threat given the elevated nature of convection, though a damaging wind gust or two are also possible. A WW issuance is not expected at this time given the anticipated isolated nature of the threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A multicellular cluster of elevated convection has recently organized into a forward propagating MCS, which is currently tracking southward across central OK. Within the past hour or so, hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter have been reported, in addition to a few damaging wind gusts. The MCS currently appears to be rooted above the boundary layer, with parcels being ingested within the 850-700 mb layer. The MCS is currently traversing the eastern edge of a LLJ axis, with 850-700 mb WAA maximized along the trajectory of the MCS in central OK. The WAA has likely been the main forcing mechanism for initiating cells that have been sustaining the MCS up to this point. The 12Z observed OUN sounding showed near 9 C/km lapse rates within the 700-500 mb layer, which will continue to support the large hail threat. Given the elevated nature of the convection, large hail is expected to be the main threat, though a couple damaging wind gusts are possible in association with downward momentum transport within the heaviest rain/hail cores. The MCS is expected to move out of the WAA regime, which may encourage a gradual weakening trend with time. As such, the severe threat appears isolated enough such that a WW issuance is not anticipated at this time.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Within Severe Thunderstorm Watch 347, a cluster of south/southeastward-moving thunderstorms will continue to pose a damaging wind/some hail risk across south-central OK. Trends are being closely monitored for the possibility of an additional Watch across North TX, which could be needed within the hour (before 1130 AM CDT).
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A south/southeastward-moving cluster (around 35 kt forward motion) with history of wind damage/periodic severe hail continues along the I-35 corridor of south-central OK, with the leading edge nearing the Wyneewood/Davis/Sulphur areas as of 1025 AM CDT. The linear cluster remains relatively well-organized with a tight leading-edge reflectivity gradient and signs of moderately strong rear inflow and a deep cold pool, with 30+ kt winds within the lowest 2-3km AGL observed in recent KTLX WSR-88D VWP data. Mid-level temperatures warm and background environmental winds, if anything, tend to weaken with southward extent. That said, a readily evident cold pool (accompanied by strong pressure rises) appears to be relatively well balanced with moist/moderately strong southerly storm-relative inflow, which may help to maintain severe-caliber storms with a damaging wind threat into parts of North TX. This is all while lapse rates will continue to steepen as low-level inhibition gradually erodes as temperatures warm through the middle/upper 80s F as of 15Z. ..Guyer.. 06/09/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms capable of damaging winds and isolated large hail will continue to spread south-southeastward across north Texas including the Metroplex through mid-afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A well-organized and relatively compact MCS continues to maintain its integrity as it progresses south-southeastward at around 35 kt early this on the north edge of the Metroplex as of 130 PM CDT. Denton TX had a measured 52 kt wind gust around 1257 PM CDT, with a more recent 62 kt wind gust (138 PM CDT) measured at Dallas Love Field. Damaging winds will remain likely these storms, and more so, the gust front that precedes these storms by several miles (10 miles in some cases). These storms will continue to favor the instability gradient south-southeastward along and parallel to the I-35 East/I-45 corridors where additional mid-level convection precedes these storms. Wind-driven large hail is also a possibility, particularly with evidence of embedded/hybrid-supercell type characteristics. Otherwise, additional storm development farther to the west will become increasingly likely through mid/late afternoon as inhibition continues to erode. ..Guyer.. 06/09/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorms will become increasing likely across western North Texas southward into much of central Texas through mid/late afternoon. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will be issued within the hour.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite imagery trends in conjunction with subjective surface analysis suggest that inhibition continues to erode with increasingly common towering cumulus across the Big Country, near and south of where south/southwestward-advancing outflow is intercepting a northeast/southwest-oriented cold front. The air mass along/east of the front is very unstable southward into Edwards Plateau/Hill Country vicinity where lower 70s F surface dewpoints are contributing to upwards of 4000 J/kg MLCAPE. Thunderstorms are likely to continue to develop and increase in coverage/intensity through the afternoon. Although low/mid-tropospheric winds are not overly strong, factors such as veering winds with height, somewhat stronger high-level westerlies, as well as very strong buoyancy could allow for some initial intense supercells. With time, storms should tend to organize into southward-moving clusters with heightened wind damage potential into a hot/very unstable environment across much of central Texas/Edwards Plateau.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe risk may continue southeastward across portions of east-central toward southeast Texas such that an additional Severe Thunderstorm Watch may be needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The easternmost portion of a long-lived quasi-linear cluster continues to steadily progress southeastward, generally centered along the I-45 corridor near the Corsicana and Athens areas as of 320 PM CDT. While the integrity of the line has somewhat lessened and clouds tops have begun to modestly warm, a surface cold pool will help maintain these storms southeastward along the instability gradient that largely parallels I-45. At least some potential for damaging winds and possibly some hail will likely continue over the next few hours, potentially into areas currently outside of Watches 348/349. Convective trends will continue to be closely monitored as a continuance of severe-caliber storms could prompt an additional Severe Thunderstorm Watch issuance for parts of east-central/southeast Texas.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe, potentially damaging wind threat will continue to shift southward across parts of western into central TX this evening, including the greater Austin metro area. Large hail also is possible. A tornado threat may persist in the short term, through damaging winds are expected to be the main concern through the evening hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An intense supercell over Coryell and Lampasas Counties has recently produced a tornado near Copperas Cove, TX. This cell has generated a few hail and strong wind reports over the last hour or so. Latest radar analysis has shown a myriad of boundaries across the vicinity including several outflow boundaries produced by the supercell itself in addition to other cells further east. Also noted were horizontal convective rolls feeding into the inflow region of the cell. These interactions are likely enhancing tornado potential locally, as well as driving further convective development westward into Llano County and eastward into Milam County. A very moist and strongly unstable airmass resides downstream of this convection with surface dewpoints in the upper 60s and low 70s with temperatures in the mid 90s to near 100 degrees F. Steep lapse rates greater than 8 deg C/km atop this moist boundary layer is aiding in MLCAPE around 3000 J/kg amidst 30-40 kt northwesterly effective shear. This environment should continue to foster organized severe convection and upscale growth into the evening hours. Visible satellite imagery shows additional deepening of cumulus westward along a prefrontal trough/convergence band and additional development is possible further west across WW 349. Given the volatile thermodynamic environment, damaging winds (some possibly significant) will remain possible the next several hours across the WW 349 area. ..Leitman.. 06/09/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat will mainly continue south of the Houston WFO across eastern portions of the Austin/San Antonio WFO in WW 350. Damaging wind and possibly some hail will be the main concerns over the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The severe threat across much of the Houston WFO has diminished this evening. A gravity wave feature was noted on visible satellite imagery, propagating across the Houston WFO earlier this evening. This appears to have had a stabilizing affect across this portion east-central/southeast Texas. Severe potential still remains possible south of the Houston WFO across southern portions of WW 350 through the remainder of the evening. Damaging winds and possibly some hail will be possible with any cells that develop across this region or as the bowing line segment further to the northwest tracks toward this area over the next couple of hours. ..Leitman.. 06/10/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A damaging wind threat will continue across WW 349 this evening. A watch replacement may be needed for WW 349 as threat may continue beyond the 03z expiration time, as well as extend south of the current watch boundary.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A severe line with bowing elements at time continue this evening just north of San Antonio and extending east-west from Bastrop to Edwards Counties. Latest measured wind gusts from KAUS have reached 66 mph, with other measured and estimated reports from 70 to 80 mph across other parts of Travis County. Additionally, isolated reports of around 1 inch hail have also been noted. Eastern portions of the line have been surging southward at around 30-40 kt while western portions of the line have a slower forward progression at about 20-30 kt. Regardless, severe gusts have been noted along the entirety of the line. Given a very warm/moist and unstable boundary layer ahead of the line, expect severe potential to continue into late evening and move outside of WW 349 and WW 350. 00z RAOB from CRP and DRT continue to show very steep lapse rates and MUCAPE greater than 4000 J/kg. While loss of daytime heating will further increase inhibition, temperatures currently in the 90s to near 100 degrees will continue to support intense downdrafts and severe threat likely will wane only slowly with time and southward extent. A new watch may be needed to replace portions of WW 349 as the threat may continue beyond the 03z expiration time. Additional counties in portions of WFO EWX and WFO CRP may need to be included in this potential new severe thunderstorm watch as well. ..Leitman.. 06/10/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Greatest severe threat through 07Z is expected to remain over the western portion of WW 351, primarily along the Rio Grande to the southeast of Del Rio.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Late this evening, most of the storms embedded within a large MCS continues to weaken especially along its eastern two thirds across south central TX. The outflow boundary has surged well ahead of most of the reflectivity cores, most likely due to a substantial increase in convective inhibition associated with stabilization of the surface layer. An exception is with the small cluster of storms southeast of Del Rio where outflow from the dying downstream storms has merged with outflow from the ongoing activity, resulting in renewed development along the southeast flank. This activity may continue to propagate south southeast through the moderately unstable environment along and just north of the northwest-southeast oriented outflow boundary next hour or two, posing a threat for damaging wind and hail before finally weakening.
